findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class body runs, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` gets the same process-start timestamp. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: `to_dict()` puts a datetime into Celery task kwargs and `from_dict` can't round-trip it
findings.body: `asdict(self)` keeps `queued` as a `datetime`. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as `apply_async` kwargs. If the broker serializer is JSON, the datetime is either rejected or turned into a string. On the receiving side, `from_dict` then builds `queued` as a string rather than a datetime. The dict is not a safe serialization format. The test only checks that `queued` is not None. Serialize `queued` to ISO format explicitly, or drop the field.

findings.title: Passing `assignment_source` kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound` breaks integrations that don't accept it
findings.body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. Implementations that lack `**kwargs`, or that reject unexpected arguments, will raise `TypeError`. The abstract signature has `**kwargs`, but the diff doesn't show that every concrete integration (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) accepts it. The PR also changes only the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature. That change is unrelated to this fix.

findings.title: Inbound sync check does not use the source, and other call sites of `should_sync` are unverified
findings.body: `where_should_sync` still calls `should_sync(key)` without a source. That is fine for inbound. But `should_sync` gained a new parameter in a base class and a subclass, and the PR does not show that every override (for example, integrations that override `should_sync`) was updated. An override with the old signature would raise `TypeError` when the task passes the second positional argument.

findings.title: Runtime import of the integrations package from the models layer
findings.body: `AssignmentSource` is imported at module level and used only as a type annotation. The import adds a runtime dependency from `sentry.models` on `sentry.integrations.services`, and `from __future__ import annotations` is already in effect. It should go under `TYPE_CHECKING` to avoid the import-cycle risk.

findings.title: No test covers the end-to-end inbound webhook path or deassign with a source
findings.body: The new tests cover only `assign` with a matching source. There is no test that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passes the source through to outbound sync. There is also none for `deassign` with a matching source, or for a non-matching source (another integration) still syncing. The task-level `from_dict` round-trip through Celery is not tested either, which is where the serialization problem would show up.
